newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Democracy groups have vowed to make sure Chavalit Yongchaiyudh keeps his promise to build a monument to those killed in the student uprising of October 14, 1973. The moves comes as city councillors and the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration agree to seek to negotiate with the government to build the monument themselves. (BANGKOK POST)

- An investigation into the leak about Narong Kittikachorn's pension has been agreed by the prime minister and the supreme commander. Chavalit Yongchaiyudh and Mongkol Ampornpisit regard the leak as deeply damaging to national unity. Exposure of Gen. Chavalit's decision to give Col. Narong a military pension has enraged democracy groups and the public and arouses strong opposition from his cabinet and the New Aspiration Party. (BANGKOK POST)

- The first meeting between governors from adjacent Thai and Laotian provinces have begun with both sides feeling optimistic over solving old problems. An informed source at the meeting says Thailand has given Laos assurances about taking swift action on problems that could affect the boundary along the Mekong River. (THE NATION)

- The Bank of Thailand has announced a variety of incentives for finance companies to merge and increase the stability and competitiveness of the financial sector. The incentives include eligibility for new retail banking operations such as the ability to accept passbook savings deposits and run foreign exchange operations, as well as permission to expand branch networks. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- The plan to rehabilitate the Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC), proposed by Industrial Finance Corporation of Thailand (IFCT), is expected to be approved by Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan today before he leaves for the United States roadshow. Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanonda has earlier approved the IFCT management plan for the ailing bank which suffers over 77 billion baht worth of non-performing loans and doubtful debts. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The eight provinces in the second stage of the Eastern Seaboard Development Programme will see hundreds of billions of baht in investment and 450,000 new jobs between now and 2006, according to the National Economic and Social Development Board (NESDB). The board will outline the second-stage development strategy at a seminar today for public and private-sector representatives. The plans are based on a study by Team Consulting Engineers Co. (BANGKOK POST)
